newsitem.title: USA: SEC responds to California muni probe request.
newsitem.headline: SEC responds to California muni probe request.

text.p: The Securities and Exchange Commission has responded to California state Treasurer Matt Fong's call for a probe of municipal bond financings in the state, Fong's office said.
Sources familiar the matter said the SEC referred Fong's request to its municipal enforcement officials.
Fong's office said the treasurer received a response last week from the SEC in Washington, but declined to release a copy of the letter or to discuss its contents.
SEC officials also declined to comment on the letter.
In September, Fong called on the SEC and California's Attorney General to investigate nine municipal securities transactions underwritten by Pacific Genesis Group Inc.
David Fitzgerald, chief executive of San Francisco-based underwriter Pacific Genesis Group, said that his firm has not been contacted by the SEC regarding Fong's letter.
"To date, we have not been contacted," he said.

In these municipal bond deals, Fong alleged that illegal payments of bond proceeds were made, bond proceeds were used to retire private debts and bond professionals failed to identify the actual project beneficiaries.
"In my view, these practices violate state laws, raise federal securities law concerns and harm the interests of the issuer community in general," Fong said in September.

The transactions were conducted under the state's Marks-Roos Local Bond Pooling Act, authorizing the formation of joint powers agencies to finance the capital projects of local governments in California.
